name: Dutch Gold Coast
alt: Nederlandse Bezittingen ter Kuste van Guinea
Dutch West India Company Gold Coast

predecessors.name: Portuguese Empire
predecessors.text: Elmina, Shama and Axim, the Portuguese forts the Dutch captured in 1637, 1640 and 1642

predecessors.name: Swedish Empire
predecessors.text: Fort Batenstein at Butri (ceded 1656) and Fort Witsen at Takoradi (Dutch from 1665), both built by the Swedes

predecessors.name: Brandenburg-Prussia
predecessors.text: Fort Dorothea and Gross Friedrichsburg (Hollandia), sold by Prussia in 1721 for 7,200 ducats

successors.name: British Gold Coast
successors.text: the Dutch forts west of Elmina and Elmina itself, handed to Britain on 6 April 1872

ledger.x: 1612: the Dutch build Fort Nassau at Moree, the first Dutch fort on the Gold Coast.
1637: the table lists Cape Coast Castle as occupied from 1637 (to 1652) with no remark; the page does not say from whom it was taken, so the counterpart is recorded as nobody.
1637: the Dutch capture Elmina from the Portuguese.
1637: the capital moves from Fort Nassau at Moree to Elmina, which it stays until 1872.
1640: the Dutch take Fort San Sebastian at Shama from the Portuguese.
1640: the table lists Fort William at Anomabu as occupied 1640-1652 with no remark; the page names no previous holder.
1642: the Dutch take Fort Santo Antonio at Axim from the Portuguese (table: 'Captured from the Portuguese').
1642: the Dutch found Fort Crevecoeur at Accra and a trading post at Sekondi (table: Fort Crevecoeur 1642; Sekondi 'Trading post established by the Dutch in 1642').
1647: the Dutch conquer the English post at Egya.
1652: Cape Coast Castle and Fort William at Anomabu pass out of Dutch hands; the table gives 1652 as the end of both occupations and no recipient, so the counterpart is nobody.
1656: the Dutch hold Fort Batenstein at Butri and sign the Treaty of Butre on 27 August.
1664: the English take Axim and Egya.
1665: De Ruyter takes Fort Amsterdam at Cormantin, the first English fort on the Gold Coast, and Axim returns to the Dutch.
1665: Fort Witsen at Takoradi becomes Dutch (table: Takoradi, Fort Witsen, 1665, 'Originally built by the Swedes').
1667: the Dutch found Fort Goede Hoop at Senya Beraku (table: 1667).
1682: the Dutch build Fort Vredenburgh at Komenda.
1687: the Dutch first occupy Fort Dorothea at Akwidaa, a Brandenburger fort.
1697: the Dutch found Fort Lijdzaamheid at Apam (table: 1697).
1698: the Dutch occupation of Fort Dorothea ends and the fort reverts to Brandenburg.
1711: the Dutch occupy Fort Dorothea again, until April 1712.
1712: the second Dutch occupation of Fort Dorothea ends in April.
1721: Prussia sells its Gold Coast to the Dutch.

1724: the Dutch take actual possession of Fort Hollandia at Princess Town, held since 1717 by the local ruler Jan Conny: table 'Up until 1724 occupied by the local Jan Conny'; Brandenburger page: Jan Conny 'occupied Gross Friedrichsburg' 1717 to 1724 despite the 1721 sale.
1734: the Dutch build Fort Singelenburgh at Keta; it is destroyed in 1737 ('Destroyed by the Dutch in 1737 after it was attacked by the local population').
1737: Fort Singelenburgh at Keta is destroyed by the Dutch themselves after an attack and abandoned.
1782: Britain seizes five Dutch forts in the Fourth Anglo-Dutch War.
1782: the Dutch capture Fort Sekondi from the British (table: 'Captured from the British in the Fourth Anglo-Dutch War'); it is given back in 1785.
1784: the Treaty of Paris returns the five forts.
1785: Fort Sekondi goes back to Britain (table: Fort Sekondi 1782-1785, 'Given back').
1811: Fort Goede Hoop at Senya Beraku is occupied by the local Akim until 1816 (table: 'occupied by the local Akim between 1811 and 1816').
1816: the Dutch regain Fort Goede Hoop from the Akim (table: occupied by the Akim 1811-1816).
1868: the forts east of Elmina pass to Britain.
1868: the British forts west of Elmina pass to the Netherlands: Beyin (Apollonia, now Fort Willem III), Dixcove (Fort Metalen Kruis), Komenda and Sekondi, effective 1 January 1868.
1868: resistance at Komenda.
1870: the Dutch punitive expedition ends.
1872: the Dutch hand Elmina to Britain.

wars.name: Battle of Elmina (1637)
wars.outcome: Dutch victory: Elmina captured from the Portuguese in August 1637, ending Portuguese rule on the Gold Coast; Shama (1640) and Axim (1642) followed.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Dutch War (Guinea theatre)
wars.outcome: The English took Axim and Egya in 1664; De Ruyter recaptured Dutch posts in early 1665 and took Fort Amsterdam at Cormantin; at Breda (31 July 1667) the Dutch kept Fort Cormantin.

wars.name: Komenda Wars
wars.outcome: Four wars over Komenda; 'little territory changed hands'; the English came out with the main trade advantage and the Dutch kept Fort Vredenburgh.

wars.name: Fourth Anglo-Dutch War (Gold Coast)
wars.outcome: Britain seized five Dutch forts in 1782 and the Dutch took Fort Sekondi; all forts went back to their pre-war owners under the Treaty of Paris of 1784.

wars.name: Ahanta War (1838)
wars.outcome: 'The disastrous Ahanta War led to a royal decree on 23 March 1838 that strengthened colonial government'; no territorial change recorded.

wars.name: Fante Confederacy siege of Elmina
wars.outcome: The confederacy's army marched on Elmina in March 1868, began the siege in April and lifted it in May; a peace treaty between the confederacy and Elmina followed in June 1868.

wars.name: Dutch Gold Coast expedition of 1869-70
wars.outcome: Dutch-led force burned the villages of Komenda, Anoema and Kwassie in December 1869 and January 1870; the Dutch won militarily but the expedition 'ended Dutch involvement on the Gold Coast'; the colony was sold to Britain in 1872.

certainty.note: A string of coastal forts with undefined hinterlands: Cliopatria's shape is a coastal strip of 17 to 86 cells around the fort sites and the pages give no boundary.
